To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel personalized multi domain algorithm for kidney stone disease diagnosis tailored to acute care, using a single center database.

we have developed a personalized diagnostic acute care model for kidney stone diseases that integrates large clinical, demographics, laboratory data; the model has a high accuracy and is interpretable.

we developed and validated a multi domain diagnostic acute care algorithm (DACA KS); it has a high sensitivity and specificity for KS; it is based on demographic, vital signs and laboratory variables; it can be integrated into clinical practice to help nurses and clinicians during triage; the algorithm can be used in the emergency department to help with triage and in acute care to streamline patient care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, personalized, and multi-domain algorithm to aid in the diagnosis and treatment of patients with acute care KS.
the development of a personalized diagnostic acute care model for KS disease tailored to acute and emergency care.
a big data approach for personalized diagnostics of KS, which could be applied to other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to infer a personalized diagnostic acute care model for KS disease.

the multi domain approach using a super learner yielded a sensitivity/specificit of 0.83/0.83, with an AUROC of.85 in cross validation, which represents an increase of 0.05 in sensitivity/specificity and 0.03 in AUROC over the STONE score.
DACA KS is a promising tool for the early identification of KS in acute care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a big data approach, using a large, diverse dataset and a collection of statistical methods, could be used to develop a personalized, multi domain diagnostic model for kidney stones tailored to acute care.
a personalized, multi domain, big data approach can be used to infer a diagnostic acute care algorithm with good performance.
the multi domain approach is able to improve the performance of the STONE score for the diagnosis of KS, while providing additional information on comorbidity and labs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multi domain personalized approach to KS diagnosis in acute care could be feasible.
the integration of large clinical, demographic and laboratory data can improve the performance of diagnostics algorithms for KS, and potentially other conditions.
big data approaches can be effectively used to develop personalized algorithms for clinical decision support in acute care.
